notes.16: The first heading required candidates to write about the two different points related to the meaning and definition of the word Yoga. Most of the candidates managed to write two correct points.
notes.17: This question asked: ‘What is the ideal climate to grow orchids in’? Several candidates managed to give two correct points.
notes.18: This question required candidates to give two points which highlighted the physical and mental aspects of Yoga. Some of the candidates were able to give two correct points.
notes.19: This question asked candidates to list three points related to the benefits of Yoga. Most of the candidates correctly mentioned three points. Exercise 4
notes.20: According to the new syllabus the text that is the basis for questions set on note-making, is also the same text on the basis of which candidates are required to write a summary in Exercise 4. It is noteworthy that despite the fact that the rubric clearly explained the basis on which the summary should be written and mentioned what points need to be included in it, most candidates did not follow the rubric. Consequently, few candidates managed to get the full four marks allocated for the content portion of this answer. This year’s rubric asked candidates to write their summary on the basis of four points: firstly, on the fact that the body gets strength to fight different illnesses; secondly, on the positive impact on memory and psychological concentration, Thirdly, on the fact that Meditation has been included in the syllabus of several schools in London, to help candidates fight stress and tension. Most candidates managed to get good marks for language. However, those who were unable to include any relevant points in their summary were not awarded any marks for language. Exercise 5
notes.21: Candidates were expected to write an e-mail to their friend who lives in a different city in order to plan a trip to their friend’s city. This exercise asked candidates to include three specific points in their e-mail: (1) highlighting their travelling plan (2) outline their feelings before meeting their friend (3) Explain an activity which they would like to carry out with their friend. Most of the candidates managed to complete this writing task well. The majority of the candidates included three points in their email and received full marks for content and also received good marks for language. Exercise 6 This year the essay topic was framed in terms of two opposite view points. However, while discussing to what extent they agreed with each view, candidates were also expected to reflect on the two opposing views on women’s liberation which was presented in the question paper vis-à-vis, (1) how women have received liberation after introducing the law of equality; (2) that despite introducing such laws women have not actually received freedom in real terms. This exercise and manner of setting the question has been done in accordance with the new syllabus which calls for not just giving a topic to candidates to write on but, also giving them two opposite views related to the topic that they must also consider while writing on the given theme. Several candidates gave some strong reasons in favour of these two opposite views. Good answers not only highlighted these reasons but also included valuable examples in support of their views. Writing in Hindi without making grammatical mistakes and spelling errors continues to be a central issue. Spellings mistakes are definitely an area of concern and should be addressed with some urgency. Improvement in this would make a positive difference to candidates’ grades. HINDI AS A
notes.key_messages: • In Exercises 1, 2 and 3 the emphasis is on reading skills. Spelling errors are tolerated provided that they do not interfere with communicating the correct answer to the Examiner. As long as the answer is clear, candidates are not required to write in full sentences. • In Exercise 3, complete sentences are expected while writing notes. • In Exercises 5 and Exercise 6, marks are awarded not only for content but also for accuracy. Therefore, it is important that candidates carefully check their work for spelling and grammatical errors.
notes.general_comments: This was the second year testing the revised syllabus of 0549 Hindi as a second language. It was reassuring to see that most candidates followed the guidelines well and most of them had written their answers within the word limit. The majority of candidates appeared to be at ease with Exercises 1, 2, 5 and 6.
